findings.issue: Task 1's description carries a technical decision that has no home in the Decisions section: "The query carries a comment recording why the two server-supplied WAL-name columns cannot smuggle terminal escapes: PostgreSQL only ever reports names that passed its `VALID_XFN_CHARS` filter (hex plus .history/.backup/.partial), so debt [029] is not widened here." This is a security decision (accept two server-supplied string columns without sanitisation, on a named PostgreSQL guarantee) plus its rationale, and none of Decisions 1-15 covers escape sequences, `VALID_XFN_CHARS` or debt [029]. A decision that exists only inside a task description is invisible to anyone reading the Decisions section and is lost when the task file is archived.
findings.fix: Add a Decision (e.g. Decision 16: "the two WAL-name columns need no escape sanitisation") with Decision / Rationale (the `VALID_XFN_CHARS` guarantee, why debt [029] is not widened) / Alternatives considered (sanitising in Go at render time, or in SQL — and why rejected). Shorten Task 1's sentence to the instruction alone: the query carries a comment pointing at that decision.

findings.issue: Task 6 modifies `top/help.go` (three help-screen lines: the new `w,W` entry moved out of the plain-switch line, and `archiver` added to the `Q` caveat) but does not list `top/help_test.go` under Files to modify, while its Verify says `go test ./top/...` covers "cycle, menu, help". `top/help_test.go` already exists and pins help entries by test on purpose — its own comment states "The built-in help is the only user-facing hotkey documentation in the project, so the Space entry, its placement and its alignment are pinned by a test rather than by review" (`Test_helpTemplate_pauseEntry`, `Test_helpTemplate_pauseLiftingActions`, `Test_helpTemplate_formatVerbs`, with the `helpEntryLine`/`descColumn` helpers). Two acceptance criteria depend on this (the help screen contains the `w,W` line, and the `Q` line lists `archiver`), so as written they are verified only by the manual stand run and Task 6's verify claim is not backed by any test file it owns.
findings.fix: Add `top/help_test.go` to Task 6's Files to modify and name the coverage in the description: a `w,W` entry test in the style of `Test_helpTemplate_pauseEntry` (exact line, placement, `descColumn` alignment against a neighbouring entry) plus an assertion that the `Q` line lists `archiver`. Add `top/help_test.go` to Files to read too if the existing helpers are to be reused.

findings.issue: Decision content is duplicated verbatim into task descriptions rather than referenced. Task 9's second sentence restates Decision 13 in full (`doc/release-notes/` as "the project's established home for user-visible breaks", "there is no existing -W documentation to update", "full CLI documentation for the doc/ tree stays out of scope") — the target file is already pinned by Files to modify. Task 10's second sentence restates Decision 9's measurement conditions (`pg_monitor`-only role, verbose mode on, concurrent recording, "since a superuser run would measure the wrong baseline"). Duplicated rationale drifts out of sync the moment either side is edited, and it is exactly what the Decisions section exists to hold.
findings.fix: Cut both to the instruction plus a pointer. Task 9: "Add the 0.12.0 release-notes entries for the breaking `-W` change, the PG 19 legacy-archive limitation and the `n/a` → `0 B` change on a missing `archive_status` directory, quoting the literal messages users will see. Target and scope per Decision 13." Task 10: "...including the cost measurement under the conditions fixed in Decision 9."

findings.issue: Decision numbering is out of order: Decision 15 ("an archive with no archiver data prints nothing") sits between Decision 13 and Decision 14. All fifteen numbers are present with no gaps and no duplicates, but the reading order does not match the numbering, which makes a cross-reference like "Decision 13" harder to follow and looks like an insertion accident.
findings.fix: Move the Decision 15 block below Decision 14, or renumber so the headings run 1-15 in document order. Then re-check the in-document cross-references (Decision 13 is cited from Task 9 and from Backward Compatibility; Decision 9 from Task 10 and from Risks).

findings.issue: Tasks 3 and 4 stay inside the 5-sentence limit but drift from WHAT/WHY into embedded justification. Task 3: "...both also justify swallowing the error text on the grounds that it contains a filesystem path — an argument that no longer applies once the function changes. Correct them in the same task: they are what a future reader would trust." This weighs an argument and, in passing, leaves it ambiguous whether the error-swallowing behaviour itself changes or only the comments do. Task 4: "...must never reach `ReportType`, which is used both as a tar-entry filter and as a view-map key — an unmapped value leaking through would produce a zero-value view and a silently empty report instead of an error" is a fail-closed requirement plus its rationale, and no Decision records it.
findings.fix: Task 3: keep the instruction ("correct the two `internal/stat/` comments that state the wrong privilege requirement and the stale filesystem-path justification") and state explicitly that the degradation behaviour is unchanged — only the comments are corrected. Task 4: keep "the mapping is a closed whitelist; an unmapped value falls through to the existing `report type is not specified` path" and move the `ReportType`/zero-value-view rationale into a short Decision, since it is the reason the whitelist is mandatory rather than a style preference.

summary: Round 2: all seven round-1 findings are resolved and none is re-reported. Verified — the Per-task verification table now runs 1-9 plus 10a/10b and every row's command matches the task it names (row 2 = PG 19 wal query, row 9 = release-notes grep); Tasks 6-8 carry the full code-writing default reviewer set (dev-code-reviewer, dev-security-auditor, dev-test-reviewer); Task 5's description drops the TestViews_Configure claim and states the real scope in 3 sentences; Task 9 targets doc/release-notes/v0.12.0.md, a real directory holding v0.8.0.md and v0.9.0.md, and Decision 13 names the same target and records why docs/roadmap-0.12.0.md was rejected; Task 8 names its three golden files explicitly, matching the existing report_record_bgwriter_pg18.golden / report_record_replslots.golden convention; Decision 9 has its Alternatives line; Decisions 13, 14 and 15 all carry the Decision/Rationale/Alternatives triad. Template compliance holds: frontmatter correct (created 2026-08-05, status draft, branch feature/017-feat-wal-archiver, size M), every required section present and non-empty, Feature size M declared in Testing Strategy, Risks a 6-row table with concrete mitigations, 10 tasks (limit 15), Final Wave carries the pre-deploy-qa task with no reviewers per the catalog, all skills and reviewers are valid catalog names, no time-based estimates, no Acceptance Criteria or TDD Anchor blocks inside tasks, no line-number references in task descriptions. Standards compliance is good: new file paths and names follow the project conventions (internal/query/archiver.go + archiver_test.go, the version-independent selector shape of io.go/replication_slots.go, report_record_*_test.go and the *_pgNN.golden naming), and patterns.md's "Adding a New View — test counts" list is covered across Tasks 5 and 6 (view_test.go, record_test.go, config_view_test.go, menu_test.go) — help_test.go is the one omission, filed above. Wave conflict scan is clean: Wave 1 file sets are disjoint — Task 3's internal/stat/postgres.go and postgres_test.go are touched by no other task in any wave, Task 1 owns internal/query/archiver*.go, Task 2 owns wal*.go, Task 4 owns cmd/report/*; Wave 2 is a single task; Wave 3's Task 7 (report/describe.go, report/report.go, report/report_test.go) and Task 8 (report/report_record_*_test.go plus the three goldens) are disjoint despite sharing a package, and Tasks 6 and 9 touch unrelated trees. Dependencies respect wave order (Tasks 6/7/8 need Task 5's registration from Wave 2; Task 8's replay needs Task 4's -W mapping from Wave 1) and there are no cycles. Zero critical findings, so status is approved. Three majors worth fixing before decomposition: a security decision that exists only inside Task 1's description, Task 6 changing top/help.go without owning top/help_test.go while its verify claims help coverage, and Decisions 9/13 duplicated verbatim into Tasks 10/9.
